title: THE NIGHT SHE FORGOT
excerpt: Her mother's hidden recordings reveal that the countdown began long before Maya received her first phone.
content:
### EPISODE 5 — THE NIGHT SHE FORGOT

**23:59:57.**

The countdown continued.

Maya stared at the laptop, unable to move.

**23:59:56.**

Her mother stood in the doorway.

Rebecca had lowered her gun. Daniel was slowly getting to his feet.

Nobody spoke.

Then Maya turned toward Evelyn.

“You said I killed my father.”

Evelyn wiped her cheeks.

“I said you need to remember what happened.”

“You said I killed him.”

“I don't know what happened that night.”

“You were there!”

Evelyn flinched.

Maya grabbed the edge of the table.

“Tell me everything. Right now.”

Evelyn looked at the laptop.

“First, shut that thing down.”

Daniel moved toward it.

“Don't touch it,” Rebecca warned.

He stopped.

The countdown reached 23:58:31.

Maya looked at the screen.

“What's going to happen when it reaches zero?”

Nobody answered.

“What's going to happen?”

Daniel finally spoke.

“The archive will restore the original memory.”

Maya looked at him.

“Restore it where?”

“Inside your head.”

“And what does that mean?”

“It means everything they removed from your memory will come back.”

Rebecca shook her head.

“Not necessarily. The process was never tested on a subject who had been disconnected for this long.”

Evelyn stepped forward.

“That's why we need to leave.”

“Where?”

“Somewhere they can't find us.”

Maya laughed without humour.

“You still think there's somewhere they can't find us?”

She looked at the camera feed.

The figure standing behind Evelyn had disappeared.

But the camera was still recording.

Someone was watching.

Someone had been watching for years.

***

At 5:12 a.m., Daniel drove them away from the apartment.

He refused to explain where they were going until they had crossed three different neighbourhoods.

Maya sat in the back seat with Rebecca.

Evelyn sat beside Daniel.

Nobody spoke for the first fifteen minutes.

Finally, Maya broke the silence.

“Where are we going?”

“Your father's old workshop,” Daniel answered.

“My father had a workshop?”

“Under the old printing building in Yaba.”

Maya looked at Rebecca.

“Did you know about this?”

Rebecca nodded.

“Your father used it before Meridian House.”

“Why didn't anyone tell me?”

“Because your father made us promise.”

Maya looked out the window.

“I'm getting tired of promises.”

Daniel turned down a narrow street.

“Your father left something there. Something that can stop the restoration.”

“What?”

“A recording.”

“Of what?”

“The original experiment.”

Maya leaned forward.

“Why didn't you give it to me before now?”

Daniel looked at her through the rear-view mirror.

“Because I didn't know whether you were ready to hear it.”

“I'm ready now.”

He said nothing.

***

The building looked abandoned.

Its windows were covered in dust, and a faded sign hung above the entrance. A broken security light flickered beside the door.

Daniel parked behind the building.

“Stay close.”

He led them through a narrow passage and stopped in front of a metal door.

There was no handle.

Instead, he pressed his thumb against a small glass panel.

A green light appeared.

The lock clicked.

Maya stared at him.

“You've been here before.”

Daniel nodded.

“Many times.”

“Doing what?”

“Making sure nobody found it.”

They entered.

The staircase descended into darkness.

At the bottom was a small room filled with old computers, boxes of documents and shelves of videotapes.

Maya recognised her father's handwriting on several labels.

She picked up one of the tapes.

**MAYA — BEFORE THE PROCEDURE.**

Her fingers tightened around it.

“Play this.”

Daniel connected an old video player to a monitor.

The recording began.

Samuel Cole appeared on the screen.

He looked exhausted.

His shirt was stained, and there was a cut above his eyebrow.

“If you're watching this, Maya, then something has gone terribly wrong.”

He paused and looked away from the camera.

“I don't know how much you'll remember. I don't know what they'll tell you. But there is one thing I need you to understand.”

He leaned closer.

“You were never supposed to be a subject.”

Maya swallowed.

“Your mother brought you to Meridian House because she believed they could help you recover from the accident. She didn't know what the project really was. None of us did at first.”

Evelyn looked down.

Samuel continued.

“They told us they were treating trauma. They said they could remove painful memories without damaging the rest of the brain. But the procedure did something else.”

He held up a photograph.

It showed a young woman lying in a hospital bed.

Maya recognised her.

It was her older sister, Anna.

Except Maya had never been told she had a sister.

“Anna was the first,” Samuel said. “She died during the experiment. They told us it was an accident. They told us her memories had disappeared.”

He lowered the photograph.

“But Anna's memories didn't disappear. They were transferred.”

Maya turned toward Evelyn.

“Who is Anna?”

Evelyn covered her mouth.

Samuel's voice continued.

“They used Anna's memories to build the archive. Then they used the archive to test whether memories could be transferred between people. When I discovered what they had done, I tried to get you out.”

He paused.

“But the damage had already begun.”

The screen flickered.

A new image appeared.

A younger Maya stood beside a hospital bed.

A girl lay beneath the sheets.

The girl's face was turned away from the camera.

Samuel spoke again.

“That night, Maya, you entered the room. You saw what they had done to Anna. You became frightened. You tried to wake her.”

The recording distorted.

Then Samuel said something that made Maya's blood run cold.

“Your sister was already dead when you arrived.”

Maya stepped closer to the screen.

“Then why do I remember—”

The video continued.

“You remember the fire. You remember the shouting. You remember me falling.”

Samuel looked directly into the camera.

“But you don't remember who started the fire.”

The recording stopped.

Nobody moved.

Maya turned toward her mother.

“Anna was my sister?”

Evelyn nodded.

“Why didn't you tell me?”

“I couldn't.”

“Why?”

“Because after the accident, you stopped speaking. You wouldn't eat. You wouldn't sleep. You kept asking for Anna.”

Evelyn began to cry.

“The doctors said the memories were hurting you. They said they could remove them.”

“And you agreed?”

“I thought I was saving you.”

Maya looked away.

“You gave them my memories.”

“I gave them permission to treat you.”

“You gave them permission to erase my sister.”

Evelyn had no answer.

***

At 7:40 a.m., Rebecca discovered another room behind the shelves.

It was locked.

Daniel tried several keys before finding one that worked.

Inside was a small metal cabinet.

On top sat a photograph of Samuel Cole.

Beneath it was a handwritten note.

**FOR MAYA. WHEN SHE IS READY.**

Maya opened the cabinet.

There was a phone inside.

An old phone with a cracked screen.

It powered on immediately.

One recorded message.

She pressed play.

Her father's voice filled the room.

“Maya, if you've reached this recording, then you have found the workshop. Good.”

He sounded calmer than he had in the other video.

“I need you to listen carefully. There are three people you must never trust.”

A pause.

“Dr. Shaw. Daniel Okafor. And the person who tells you that Anna is dead.”

Maya looked at Daniel.

He looked confused.

Samuel continued.

“Dr. Shaw controls the archive. Daniel helped him build it. But the third person is the most dangerous because she knows what happened before the first experiment.”

Maya's eyes moved toward Evelyn.

Her mother was standing near the door.

The recording continued.

“She was there the night Anna died.”

Evelyn began shaking her head.

“No.”

Samuel's voice became quieter.

“She knows who started the fire.”

Maya turned slowly.

“Mum?”

Evelyn backed away.

“No, Maya. Please.”

“Who started the fire?”

Evelyn looked at the phone.

Then at her daughter.

“I did.”

The room went silent.

Maya felt her knees weaken.

“What?”

Evelyn covered her face.

“I was trying to destroy the records. I thought if I burned the room, they would lose everything. I didn't know Anna was inside.”

Maya shook her head.

“You killed her?”

“I didn't know!”

“You killed my sister!”

“I was trying to save you both!”

Maya stepped forward.

“You let me believe I was responsible.”

Evelyn started crying harder.

“They told me you would never recover if you remembered what happened. They said the guilt would destroy you.”

“So you let me carry it without knowing why?”

Evelyn reached for her.

Maya moved away.

“Don't touch me.”

***

At 9:03 a.m., Daniel's phone rang.

He answered.

For a few seconds, he listened without speaking.

Then his face changed.

“What do you mean she's gone?”

Rebecca stood.

“Who?”

Daniel ended the call.

“Dr. Shaw has been found dead.”

Maya stared at him.

“Where?”

“At Meridian House.”

Rebecca lowered her eyes.

“That's impossible.”

Daniel looked at her.

“Why?”

“Because Shaw was here.”

Nobody spoke.

Maya remembered the video.

The figure standing behind her mother.

The dark shirt.

The black gloves.

She looked at the laptop.

“Show me the recording from the apartment again.”

Daniel connected his phone to the monitor and opened the saved video.

They watched it frame by frame.

The figure entered behind Evelyn.

His face appeared.

It was Dr. Shaw.

But something was wrong.

Maya moved closer.

“Stop.”

Daniel paused the recording.

She pointed at the man's left hand.

“Zoom in.”

The image became grainy.

There was a ring on his finger.

A silver ring with a black stone.

Maya looked at Evelyn.

Her mother was wearing the same ring.

Evelyn quickly pulled her hand behind her back.

Rebecca raised her pistol.

“Take it off.”

“Mum,” Maya whispered. “Why are you wearing his ring?”

Evelyn didn't answer.

Daniel stepped between them.

“Everyone calm down.”

Then his phone rang again.

This time, the caller ID displayed a name.

**DR. SHAW.**

Daniel stared at it.

The phone continued ringing.

Maya whispered, “Answer it.”

Daniel pressed the screen.

“Hello?”

A man's voice came through.

“Good morning, Daniel.”

Daniel went pale.

“Who is this?”

The voice laughed.

“You know exactly who this is.”

Maya moved closer.

“Put it on speaker.”

Daniel did.

The voice continued.

“Tell Maya that her mother is lying.”

Evelyn began shaking.

“Tell her that I never died.”

Maya's eyes widened.

“Who are you?”

A pause.

Then the voice answered.

“I'm Samuel Cole.”

Maya couldn't breathe.

“Dad?”

“I'm sorry, sweetheart.”

She grabbed the phone.

“Where are you?”

“Not far.”

“Are you alive?”

A quiet laugh.

“That's a complicated question.”

“Come and see me.”

“I can't.”

“Why?”

“Because the man you watched in that recording wasn't Dr. Shaw.”

Maya looked at the frozen image on the monitor.

The man in the black shirt.

The ring.

Her mother.

Samuel spoke again.

“That was me.”

Evelyn collapsed into a chair.

Maya looked at her.

Then back at the phone.

“You were in our apartment?”

“Yes.”

“Why didn't you come out?”

“Because I needed to know which one of them would recognise me.”

Maya's voice trembled.

“Which one?”

Samuel was silent for several seconds.

Then he said:

“Your mother.”

The call ended.

***

At 11:59 a.m., the laptop screen changed.

The countdown had disappeared.

A new message appeared.

**RESTORATION CANCELLED.**

Maya stared at it.

For the first time in days, she felt a small wave of relief.

Then another message appeared.

**SUBJECT 014 HAS REMEMBERED THE WRONG NIGHT.**

Below it was a photograph.

A photograph of Maya standing outside Meridian House.

Beside her was Anna.

Alive.

Maya's hands began to shake.

The date on the photograph was yesterday.

She zoomed in.

Anna was looking directly at the camera.

And behind her stood a man wearing a silver ring.

Samuel Cole.

The phone vibrated.

A final message arrived.

**YOUR SISTER IS ALIVE.**

Then:

**AND SHE IS COMING FOR YOU.**

END OF EPISODE 5
